Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates scattered pulmonary nodules, including a distinct nodule in the left lower lobe (visible on the lateral view), with no evidence of hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. This pattern of multiple nodules without adenopathy is characteristic of pulmonary hyalinizing granuloma, distinguishing it from sarcoidosis (which typically presents with bilateral lymphadenopathy) and metastatic disease.
